statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk of 12% remains well below the block threshold while cross-asset stress stays extreme on crude and the long end of the Treasury curve.
recommendation: Conditions are described as two-way and mean-reverting at the assessment cutoff. The narrow evidence-based danger window falls on the September 10 producer price and jobless claims release and the US cash open that follows it.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds mid-range as Brent clears $100 and the 10-year prints a 2023-era high
body: At the assessment cutoff NQ front-month futures trade 29,446.50, -0.31% against the 29,538.75 settle, 113 points above the 29,333.00 session low and 187 points below the 29,633.75 high; cash NDX is 29,432.26, -0.26%, sitting essentially on its 29,431.94 open after trading a 29,334.40-29,563.60 range. The session has therefore retraced from both extremes rather than extending one way, which is the specific evidence that keeps tail risk in the low band. Cross-asset stress, by contrast, is extreme. Brent trades near $101.10 (+3.25%) and WTI near $96.02 (+3.15%) after US forces destroyed five Iranian crude tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island, Iran retaliated against a Jordanian base and shipping, and Tehran closed the Strait of Hormuz against a standing US naval blockade. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.833% with a 4.794-4.857% day range, its highest since October 2023, after the Treasury tripled its 10- to 20-year buyback operation to $6bn; the 30-year is near 5.3%. Rate expectations have turned hawkish, with a September hike now materially priced. VIX at 16.24 is up 3.3% but off its 16.68 session high and remains historically contained, and index internals are split rather than uniformly weak: semiconductors are broadly higher while megacaps divide sharply between META and the rest. That combination of an intact two-way range, a contained volatility surface and genuinely severe macro inputs is scored as extreme stress with low tail. The dominant mode is mixed. Delayed cross-asset context was reviewed as supporting evidence only and did not drive the current-hour assessment.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours were quiet through the US evening and the Asian session, with tail between 5% and 9% and stress in the high band. Stress climbed steadily through the European morning as crude cleared $100 and Treasury yields extended, and tail peaked at 20% in the 12:00Z hour on a trend-down European tape before easing back into the low-to-mid teens once the US cash session produced genuine two-way price discovery. The 10:00Z hour has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The remainder of the US session carries a modest conditional lift into the 20:00Z cash close, where closing-auction imbalance is the peak near-term checkpoint. Overnight conditional tail returns to the single-digit baseline absent a fresh Middle East or crude headline, with the Hormuz closure the standing gap risk. The horizon's highest conditional risk sits on September 10 between the 12:30Z producer price and jobless claims release and the 13:30Z US cash open, where the WATCH state is mapped; conditional tail then decays through the US morning into the 17:00Z 30-year auction. No future price path or release outcome is asserted anywhere in this forecast.

The session has retraced from both extremes, so tail holds at 12 while cross-asset stress stays extreme.
